references.text: The formerly blind man answers Jesus' question about whether he believes in the Son of Man by saying, 'I believe, Lord,' and worships him. This is the direct fulfillment of the question in verse 35.
Jesus' self-reference as 'the Son of Man' in a previous healing story (at the Pool of Siloam) where he has authority to judge and save, paralleling the situation in chapter 9.

Jesus' first use of the title 'the Son of Man' in the Gospel of John, where he links the title to heaven opening and angels ascending and descending over the Son of Man, a central theme for the identity he reveals in chapter 9.

Nicodemus is told that the Son of Man must be lifted up so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. This is the theological context for the question about belief in the Son of Man in chapter 9.
The crowd asks, 'Who is this Son of Man?', reflecting the confusion and challenge regarding the identity of the Son of Man that Jesus presents to the outcast man.
